title: Modi heads to Manila for ASEAN summits; MEA cannot confirm a Quad leaders’ meeting
dek: The Prime Minister is in the Philippines from 16 to 18 November. Maritime security, the South China Sea and a review of the ASEAN trade pact are on India's agenda.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi will travel to Manila on Monday for the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit and the East Asia Summit, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said on Thursday, but it could not confirm whether the leaders of the Quad, the grouping of India, the United States, Japan and Australia, will meet there.

Rudrendra Tandon, the MEA's Secretary (East), told a special briefing in New Delhi that the visit would run from 16 to 18 November, with maritime security and trade and investment the main focus. The Philippines, which chairs the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) this year, hosts both summits on 17 November. Mr Modi will also attend a dinner given by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and hold bilateral meetings, Mr Tandon said.

## The Quad question

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said last month that the four Quad countries had agreed to hold a leaders' summit on the margins of the ASEAN meetings in the Philippines, according to reports. US President Donald Trump, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese are all expected in Manila.

Mr Tandon would not confirm it. "This is a programme that is quickly being developed and we don't have information as of now about it, except that the PM is attending the ASEAN meet in the Philippines," he said. MEA officials said it would be wrong to conclude that Washington had lost interest in the Quad, reports said. The MEA also did not say whether Mr Modi would meet Mr Trump.

If it happens, it would be the first Quad leaders' meeting since September 2024 in Wilmington, Delaware. India was due to host the next summit in 2025, but it did not take place. A trade agreement between India and the US has still not been signed.

## The South China Sea and China

The East Asia Summit brings ASEAN's members together with China, the US, Russia, Japan, India and others. The Philippine government has said at least 19 leaders will attend, among them Chinese Premier Li Qiang, according to reports.

Mr Tandon repeated India's position that the South China Sea must remain open to international trade and commerce. Asked about the code of conduct that ASEAN and China have been negotiating for years, he said India had no clear assessment of progress, and that any agreement must be consistent with international maritime law and respect the rights of countries that are not party to it. Diplomats in the region expect the talks to miss their end-2026 target, reports said.

India and the Philippines have deepened defence ties in recent years: Manila signed a $375 million contract in 2022 for three shore-based batteries of the India-Russia BrahMos cruise missile, and its defence secretary has said Manila wants more, according to reports.

## Trade and Myanmar

India's trade with ASEAN is about $122 billion a year, with imports from the bloc of more than $80 billion, a gap New Delhi wants to narrow through a review of the ASEAN-India Trade in Goods Agreement (AITIGA), in force since 2010. Mr Tandon said India wanted the review finished "as soon as possible" but that talks needing all members' consent take time.

On Myanmar, which shares a 1,643-km border with India's north-east and will be represented in Manila only by a foreign ministry official, he said: "There is no alternative to engaging Myanmar." Isolating the country, he said, was "not the right approach".

## What happens next

Mr Modi leaves for Manila on 16 November. The ASEAN-India and East Asia summits are on 17 November. Any Quad meeting would be announced separately. Mr Modi and Mr Trump are also expected to meet at the G20 summit in Florida in mid-December, according to reports.
